newsitem.title: INDIA: India needs $55.9 mln investment to revamp ports.
newsitem.headline: India needs $55.9 mln investment to revamp ports.

text.p: India must invest two billion rupees ($55.9 million) to develop and upgrade its smaller ports over the next five years, Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman said on Thursday.
"The government of India has projected a demand of two billion rupees in the 9th plan (over the years 1997 to 2002) for development of minor ports in the country," Venkatraman said in a statement.
India has courted foreign and private investment to spruce up its infrastructure facilities as part of an economic reform programme that began in 1991.
The productivity of the ports grew by seven to ten percent over the last five years despite the capacity constraints, the transport ministry statement said.
"Indian shipping tonnage has grown appreciably over the years and the 8th plan target of 7.0 million GRT has been achieved one year in advance," Venkatraman said.
The foreign exchange savings of the shipping industry as a whole had risen to 32.12 billion rupees during 1995/96 from 26.53 billion in the previous year, he said.
The statement said clear and transparent guidelines for private sector investments had been issued last month to expedite investments in the port sector.

The government also proposing to involve the private sector in developing about 4,000 kms (2,500 miles) of high density four-lane highways, 40 bridges, 30 by-passes and several rail over bridges, the minister said.
